name: Voice Hold
description:
Hold a key and speak. Offline dictation, text arrives as you talk.

Hold the shortcut (Ctrl+Space by default), speak, release: the words are typed in the text field under your cursor while you talk, block by block, with a grey live preview. A quick tap keeps listening hands-free (tap again, Escape or a few seconds of silence stop it). A small pill slides out of the top bar while you dictate, with the microphone level and the live text, and goes back into it when you stop.

Everything runs on your computer, offline: French, English and 23 other European languages are recognised with punctuation (Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 through sherpa-onnx). No account, no network, no cloud. An optional local LLM (Ollama) can polish each block; it is off by default.

The speech engine is a separate download (Python, GPL, about 500 MB with its models) that cannot be part of this package; nothing works without it. The extension installs it for you: a notification and the settings open an Installation page with one Install button, no terminal and no password, and a field to try the dictation in. Requires PipeWire and Python 3.12 or newer. Wayland only; applications must use the GNOME input method (GTK, Qt, Electron with Wayland; terminals get the text without the preview).
